ruling.recommended_action: Uphold the $5.00 no-show fee; no refund, no account flag on either party, no driver reminder (no route/notice issue arises).
ruling.reasoning:
The driver cancelled at 21:32:00 with the app reason rider_no_show [F4]. NS-0 asks whether his own words show a reason of his own (NS-3) rather than the rider's failure to appear [NS-0]. His chat says he is waiting at Gate B and cannot stop at Gate A because of a double yellow line, then "More than 5 min already, I have to cancel" [F10][F12][F13], and his statement repeats that he pressed "I'm Here", messaged and called, waited over five minutes and cancelled [F16]. No car trouble, other job, personal matter or refusal of the trip appears anywhere; he declined to relocate within the pickup area, but that concerns where the car waited, which NS-1 (i)–(iv) already settle and which NS-0 excludes as a "reason of his own" [F11][F12][F16][NS-0]. So the cancellation was for the rider not showing: met.

The NS-1 checklist is settled by code and passes on every limb: arrival confirmed by the "I'm Here" tap at 21:26:00 within 200 m (150 m, closest approach 40 m) [F1][F7]; the free wait run from arrival to cancellation ran 360 s against the 300 s threshold [F6][F7]; before cancelling the driver sent three in-app messages from 21:26:30 and made one in-app call at 21:27:30 [F5]; and his continuous presence at one point 150 m from the pickup for 21:26:00–21:32:00, inside 200 m for 6 min 0 s after the tap, leaves no GPS gap [F3][F7]. No 8-minute threshold is on record, so the later-of-two rule leaves the 5-minute wait satisfied [F4][F6][NS-1]. The tap was made from 150 m, not at the kerb, but the arrival test is the recorded tap with GPS inside the 200 m radius, which the GPS confirms [F1][F2][F7][NS-1].

Because all four NS-1 conditions hold, NS-2's voiding trigger is never reached and the $5.00 fee on record stands [F4][F8][NS-2]. The fee is the fixed no-show charge, so there is no excess-distance or surge arithmetic to run: the trip carried 1.0× surge and the cancellation fee of $5.00 is exactly the amount NS-1 §2.2 transfers to the driver [F8][F9][NS-1]. The rider's clean profile and the driver's clean record [F20][F21] do not change the checklist, and with no prior no-show on the rider's record NS-9 is not engaged [F20][NS-9].

Safety screen: I read every chat line and the complaint. The messages are logistics only — where the driver is, a request to come to Gate A, a refusal to stop on a double yellow line, a notice of cancellation [F10][F11][F12][F13] — and the complaint reports a refused approach and a charge, not any threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous driving [SAFE-1]. Read in context, nothing there is abuse aimed at the other party. Finding: none [F10][F11][F12][F13][F14].

Evidence: the record settles everything the ruling needs — a timestamped complete chat, GPS coverage with no gap, and the recorded arrival tap and cancellation time [F2][F3][F6][F14]. So the ruling can execute as a system-final $5.00 no-show decision [TH-1][TH-2].

No NS-1 condition fails, so NS-2's voiding trigger is never reached and the $5.00 charge stands [F4][F8][NS-1][NS-2]. The traffic and weather facts are irrelevant to a no-show test [F17][F18][F19].

A clean rider profile does not create an NS-1 condition, and the driver's record is equally clean [F20][F21]. The $5.00 fixed fee is decided finally by the system, and the checklist outcome is no_action [F8][TH-1][TH-2][NS-1].

The conclusion is accepted (no reason of his own appears [F10][F12][F13][F16][NS-0]) but it cannot rest on the app's rider_no_show label alone, which is the driver's claim; his own words are what decide the reason [F4][F13][F16][NS-0].
Agreed as a screening conclusion: the chat and complaint contain no threat, intimidation, harassment or dangerous-driving allegation [F10][F11][F12][F13][F14][SAFE-1].
